arguments.name: op
arguments.text: A character string specifying the test: -f, -d, -L, -h, -x, -w, -r, -nt, or -ot.

origin.details: Existence means the path is reachable by stat. For -x on Windows see file.access.
origin.example:
dir <- file.path(R.home(), "library", "stats")
file_test("-d", dir)
file_test("-nt", file.path(dir, "R"), file.path(dir, "demo"))

arguments.name: op
arguments.text: A character string specifying the test: -f, -d, -L, -h, -x, -w, -r, -nt, or -ot.

arguments.name: x, y
arguments.text: File paths as a string or sequence of strings.

translation.details: Existence means the path is reachable by stat, with tilde expansion like R.
translation.value: A bool or list of bools.
translation.example:
from utils.file_test import file_test
import os
r_home = os.environ.get("R_HOME", "/usr/lib/R")
dir = os.path.join(r_home, "library", "stats")
file_test("-d", dir)
file_test("-nt", os.path.join(dir, "R"), os.path.join(dir, "demo"))
